posts.title: MCU-BN-20261009-02 | Marconi USSOCOM Orion X604 | REVIEW DRAFT
posts.caption:
Marconi Technologies says it has received an initial USSOCOM contract for Orion X604 tactical radios, with deliveries expected to begin in late 2026.

The company says the radios connect operators with sensors and autonomous systems, supporting robotic control and sensor-data transfer in contested environments.

Illustrative archive: military communications training, Djibouti, Jan. 18, 2019. This is not the Orion X604 or footage of this award.
Photo: U.S. Air Force / Tech. Sgt. Thomas Grimes, via DVIDS.

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

Source: Marconi Technologies release, Oct. 9, 2026, via European Security & Defence.
https://euro-sd.com/2026/10/news/cyber-coms/54288/marconi-technologies/

posts.title: MCU-BN-20261010-01 | Lockheed Martin PAC-3 Edge | Approved
posts.caption:
Lockheed Martin has unveiled PAC-3 Edge, its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition.

The company says the interceptor adds a new seeker, a Northrop Grumman multi-pulse rocket motor and upgraded flight controls. Testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

Photo: PAC-3 MSE archive dated July 1, 2024, via Darrell Ames/U.S. Army and DVIDS. The image shows the earlier MSE variant, not PAC-3 Edge.

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

Source: Lockheed Martin, Oct. 9, 2026.
https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2026-10-09-Lockheed-Martin-Debuts-PAC-3-Edge-TM-for-the-U-S-Armys-Innovative-Future-Interceptor-Program

posts.title: MCU-ICYMI-20261009-01 | Five defense-tech developments | Approved r3
posts.caption:
ICYMI: five defense-tech developments this week.

• Anduril: $3.7B in private shipyard investment, alongside Navy work valued up to $2.9B.

• Raytheon: an SM-3 IB interceptor production and sustainment award valued up to $6.3B.

• Lockheed Martin: next-generation Army network integration with industry partners.

• Kratos: more than $100M in space and cyber mission awards.

• BLADE: Hunter WOLF advances to Phase II of the Army’s GroundBreaker 1 demonstration.

Sources: Anduril (Oct. 6), RTX (Oct. 8), Lockheed Martin (Oct. 8), Kratos (Oct. 5), HDT/BLADE (Oct. 8), 2026.

posts.title: MCU-P03 Drone Crucible 26.3
posts.caption:
Drone Crucible 26.3 put the Florida National Guard and joint partners through an integration test at Camp Blanding, Sept. 26–Oct. 2.

In its Oct. 6 report, the Guard described combining Tactical Assault Kit location data, unmanned-system information and video feeds into a shared operational picture. It also connected exercise information with higher-level commands.

The less visible requirement was technical support: the Guard said dedicated specialists were critical to maintaining that shared picture and fixing issues. Our takeaway: useful drone capability depends on connected systems and people who can keep them working.

Photo: Camp Blanding, Oct. 1, 2026. U.S. Air National Guard photo by Staff Sgt. N.W. Huertas / DVIDS.

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

Source: https://www.army.mil/article/295987/florida_national_guard_advances_unmanned_systems_during_drone_crucible_26_3

posts.title: MCU-BN-20261010-02 | Microchip acquires VORAGO | Approved
posts.caption:
Microchip Technology has acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and the company’s HARDSIL process technology to its space and defense portfolio.

The deal brings chip-design and radiation-hardening expertise for electronics that operate in harsh environments. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Source: Microchip Technology, Oct. 9, 2026.
https://ir.microchip.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1419/microchip-technology-acquires-vorago-technologies

Illustrative archive: Space Development Agency satellite-network graphic, Sept. 28, 2020, via U.S. Naval Research Laboratory/DVIDS. No VORAGO component or involvement in the pictured network is established.

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.
